en: The longest continuous record of Earth imaging in history — Landsat 1 launched 1972 (originally as ERTS-1), continuing through Landsat 9 (2021). Currently operational pair Landsat 8 (2013) + Landsat 9 (2021) at 705 km sun-synchronous orbit, 98.2° inclination. 30 m multispectral resolution. NASA builds + launches; USGS operates and distributes data. Free public access since 2008 turned Landsat into the global reference dataset for climate change, deforestation, and urban growth.

en: A pressure suit on the Moon is really a spacecraft you wear — the smallest crewed vehicle Apollo built, sized for one. The A7L had to do everything a capsule does — hold pressure, supply oxygen, carry away heat and exhaled carbon dioxide, shield against a temperature swing of hundreds of degrees between sunlight and shadow — while still letting a person kneel, walk, and pick up a rock. Those two demands fight each other, because anything holding pressure wants to go stiff as a balloon. Its answer was twenty-one layers built around a rubber-coated bladder, with the backpack making the whole thing self-contained for hours. It was the first suit rated to walk on another world, and for its missions it was the only thing between a human being and vacuum.

en: The Mercury-Redstone was a weapon taught to carry a passenger. Its ancestor was the German V-2, and its direct parent an Army ballistic missile built to deliver a warhead — now modified, softened, and made just reliable enough to trust with a human life. It could manage only a suborbital arc; it never had the power to reach orbit. en: The Lunar Rover was the first car on another world, and its entire reason to exist was reach. On foot, an astronaut can't stray far from the lander — walk too far out and you can't walk back if the suit starts to fail. Building it was its own puzzle — it had to fold flat into a wedge on the side of the Lunar Module, unfold on the surface, then drive through abrasive dust and hundreds of degrees of temperature swing on wire-mesh wheels and battery power. It never went fast. It went far, and that was the whole point.

en: Buran was the Soviet Union's answer to the Space Shuttle — outwardly almost identical, but with two decisions that arguably bettered the original: it carried no main engines (all the lift came from the separate Energia rocket), and it could fly with no one aboard. It was a flawless flight and its only one. The Soviet Union collapsed, the money and the mission vanished, and Buran was cancelled — the flown orbiter later crushed when its hangar roof fell in 2002. One of the most impressive and most pointless achievements in spaceflight.
